questions.explanation: 'Were' inverts with the subject in formal conditionals, replacing 'if ... were'.
questions.q: ___ hesitate, the opportunity would be lost.

questions.explanation: The past perfect 'had known' marks the unreal past; 'would have known' is wrong in the if-clause.
questions.q: ___ the danger, I would have warned you.

questions.explanation: Formal 'should' inverts with the subject for an unlikely future condition.
questions.q: ___ further information, please contact the office.

questions.explanation: 'Were it not for' is the formal inverted form of 'if it were not for'.
options: If it were not for it
questions.q: ___ your intervention, the deal would have collapsed.
Choose the correct unreal past sentence.
options: If she had studied, she would have passed.
If she would have studied, she would have passed.
If she had studied, she would pass.
Had she studied, she will have passed.
questions.explanation: The third conditional needs past perfect in the if-clause and 'would have' in the main clause.
'Had it not been for' is the formal inverted third conditional with a noun phrase.
options: If it had not been for
questions.q: ___ the storm, the rescue would have succeeded.

questions.explanation: The mixed conditional pairs a past condition with a present result: past perfect + 'would' + base.
options: If he took the job, he will be
If he had taken the job, he would be
If he had taken the job, he would have been
Were he to take the job, he would have been
questions.q: ___ wealthier now. (past condition, present result)

questions.explanation: In formal hypotheticals, 'were' is preferred over 'was' with all subjects.
questions.q: ___ to resign, who would replace him?

questions.explanation: 'But for' introduces a formal unreal condition equivalent to 'if it were not for'.
questions.q: ___ your generosity, the project would never have started.

questions.explanation: Formal inversion requires 'had' + subject + past participle, without 'if'.
questions.q: ___ me sooner, I could have intervened.
Select the correct sentence.
options: If the talks would fail, sanctions would follow.
If the talks failed, sanctions would follow.
If the talks would have failed, sanctions would follow.
If the talks fail, sanctions would follow.
questions.explanation: The second conditional uses past simple in the if-clause, not 'would'.
'Were to' + inversion expresses a remote hypothetical future formally.
questions.q: ___, the region might stabilise.

questions.explanation: Only the 'had ... would have' form correctly marks both clauses as unreal past.
options: Had they invested, they would have profited
Had they invested, they would profit
If they would have invested, they profited
Had they invest, they would have profited
questions.q: Choose the correct sentence.

questions.explanation: 'Were I in your position' is the formal inverted second conditional.
options: If I am in your position
If I would be in your position
questions.q: ___, I would decline.
Choose the correct unreal past result.
options: If the scandal had broken, she will have resigned.
If the scandal had broken, she would have resigned.
If the scandal had broken, she would resign.
If the scandal had broken, she had resigned.
questions.explanation: The unreal past result needs 'would have'; 'will have' wrongly suggests a real future.
'Had there been' inverts the existential 'there' in a formal unreal past conditional.
questions.q: ___ earlier warnings, lives could have been saved.

questions.explanation: The main clause of a second conditional uses 'would' + base verb, not 'will'.
questions.q: If the board met today, it ___ the proposal.

questions.explanation: Only one option pairs the inverted past perfect with the correct modal result.
options: Should he have known, he warned us
Had he known, he would have warned us
Had he known, he will have warned us
If he had known, he warns us
questions.q: Which sentence is grammatically correct?

questions.explanation: 'Were it to' + inversion marks a highly unlikely future condition in formal prose.
questions.q: ___ during the ceremony, the event would be moved indoors.

questions.explanation: The mixed conditional contrasts a past condition with a present result using 'would' + base.
options: If you had slept, you would feel
If you slept, you would have felt
If you would have slept, you feel
questions.q: ___ better now. (past condition, present result)
